checks_run: Inventoried all candidate files, file types, permissions, and sealed-material paths.
Parsed MANIFEST.yaml and PROVENANCE.json as JSON and cross-checked project, source, commit, status, and production fields.
Recomputed the byte-level SHA-256 digest of PROVENANCE.json and compared it with MANIFEST.yaml provenance_sha256.
Attempted the public test, sealed reference test, and benchmark scripts under independent 10-second time bounds.
Ran POSIX shell syntax checks on all submitted runner scripts.
Ran an independent read-only delimiter, lexical-state, package-path, and public-type filename sanity scan over 25 Java files.
Statically reviewed the starter API, reference lexer/parser/analyzer/emitter, public and sealed tests, adversarial cases, exercises, and validation prose.
Inspected learner-view separation, generated-material licensing, provenance declarations, runner isolation, and common credential signatures.
Compared a deterministic candidate tree digest before and after test attempts to confirm the submitted material was unchanged.
evidence: REVISE: MANIFEST.yaml declares provenance_sha256 0577e5701f5f7125eb6b8c378a0607e95cd98d1253e257593d3b7e739a69319a, but the submitted PROVENANCE.json bytes hash to 7945a3a2b470aff1edc4a632444e43ae0f44bf33b5f2511fc2f5c15e0e8e3797.

The declared manifest hash equals PROVENANCE.json's embedded snapshot_sha256 field, but that field-to-field equality does not authenticate the provenance file; the candidate's immutable metadata binding PASS wording is therefore unsupported as written.

java, javac, ecj, jikes, jshell, and Java parser substitutes were unavailable. The three Java runners each exited 127 before compilation, execution, or measurement, so no BUILDS, TESTED, or BENCHMARKED evidence was produced.
MANIFEST.yaml honestly remains status GENERATED with validation_labels GENERATED and PARTIAL, independent_validation REQUIRED, and productionized false.
The independent static Java sanity scan passed for 25 files, and shell syntax passed for all three runners; neither result establishes Java compilation or JVM bytecode correctness.
The submission contains 24 sealed/reference/answer files. No deterministic learner export manifest or transfer-verification evidence demonstrates that these files are excluded from the learner view.
All three runner scripts invoke javac/java without their own timeout, resource bound, process-group control, or captured-log contract; the reviewer supplied an outer 10-second timeout.
LICENSE_BOUNDARY.md candidly marks the linked resource NOASSERTION and says it was not copied, but the independently generated artifact has no explicit license grant or SPDX identifier.
The candidate tree digest was c3c9eb94a71f25b9695cf39ff6966d7349a621e4b4f4b5d22fd59cd34a7e1bb5 both before and after bounded runner attempts.
limitations: No Java compiler or JVM was available, so source compilation, generated-class loading, verifier behavior, runtime semantics, determinism, defensive-copy behavior, limits, and benchmark behavior remain inconclusive.

The upstream catalog checkout, linked article, and authoritative ingestion database were outside the review workspace; catalog CC0 evidence and the no-copy/no-paraphrase declaration could not be independently established from submitted files alone.
No harness-produced learner projection was provided, so progressive-disclosure transfer isolation could only be assessed from paths and prose, not verified end to end.
The credential scan covered common signatures only and is not a general secret detector.
No fuzzing, mutation testing, cross-JDK verification, performance measurement, production review, or transfer verification was performed.
